feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-heavy roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and overstuffed with overlapping skills sections, which slightly weakens clarity and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization show trust, growth, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good use of scale and specifics: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms add impact and believability.  
- Strong positioning for digital strategy roles: summary, experience, and technical skills consistently support a senior cross-channel communications profile.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, conversions, or team performance where possible.  
- Minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is slightly inconsistent (e.g., “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “French (A2/Learning)” would read more professionally as “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the experience section, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding a clearer leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with seniority and outcomes: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience shaping web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations.”
- Replace generic phrases like “Expert in” with sharper wording: “Leads cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and editorial/workflow systems that improve coordination, governance, and audience reach.”
- Keep the final sentence concise and distinctive: “Brings deep experience in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” closely repeat Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” and “advocacy messaging” are reinforced throughout Work Experience, so avoid overexplaining them here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/technical strengths will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, CV-aligned language: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication”; “Web platform governance & CMS administration” instead of “Web & CMS administration.”
- Reorder for relevance/recency: Digital strategy & transformation • Editorial systems & governance • Web platform modernization • Analytics & performance reporting • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Combine overlapping items: merge “Editorial workflow design” with “Workflow & systems architecture” into “Editorial systems, workflows & governance.”
- Keep style consistent with other sections by using plural nouns where appropriate: “communications,” “systems,” “analytics.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills almost exactly.
- “Digital strategy & transformation” and “Policy & advocacy communication” repeat the header summary and Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project footer. Tighten it around 4–5 high-impact outcomes and add scale/results where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into outcome-oriented bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance for coordinated cross-channel communications.
- Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level if those projects stay.
- Governance/analytics/workflow language also overlaps with the summary and NACo role.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. To sharpen it, lead with enterprise impact, tighten channel-management language, and add outcomes beyond platform size where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite the website bullet to emphasize transformation + scale: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel and analytics bullets outcome-driven: add email performance, audience growth, reporting adoption, decision speed, or efficiency gains if available.
- Combine governance/operations language for concision: “Established digital governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the earlier Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on enterprise oversight, not day-to-day channel management.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer project examples; keep the CV item at leadership/organizational-impact level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to executional leadership and channel growth, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built cross-functional editorial planning processes linking communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and coordination.
- If possible, add metrics: newsletter open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround-time improvements, or audience growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is too close to the Director role’s “Led NACo’s digital communications team.”
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the leadership scope and emphasize distinctive strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, more senior wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations & publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy, content planning & storytelling
- Consider combining “editorial systems and governance” with “audience-focused content planning” to reduce list sprawl.
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact areas from current/NACo roles: enterprise web modernization, governance, campaign platforms, AI-enabled discovery.
- Keep noun phrases parallel; avoid mixing abstract strategy terms with execution-level wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is also echoed in Core Competencies; refine it or swap for a more differentiated strength.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, make it more strategic, grouped, and tied to the recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” instead of listing platforms first.
- Group related items and trim lower-priority terms: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages” / “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)” / “API integrations & workflow automation” / “Airtable-based systems” / “AI-enabled search experiences.”
- Put the most relevant recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, sharpen with scope language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “Public-sector web platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave exhaustive tools to the technical section.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a senior-level capability statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and elevate the content to: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If you have metrics, connect this skill set to outcomes elsewhere in experience bullets (e.g. improved decision-making, reporting adoption, or performance gains), rather than here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep this section strategic and let Technical + IT hold the fuller tools list.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader digital strategy unless tied to analytics/optimization specifically.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Multimedia & Creative Tools.” Tighten it to emphasize delivery capability and higher-value production leadership rather than generic task terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more outcome-oriented phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the in-house studio build noted in recent experience.
- Shorten “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “Hybrid and virtual event delivery” for stronger execution language.
- If space allows, add one higher-level term like “Run-of-show production” or “Technical direction” only if you’ve done it directly.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- Tool-specific detail here may overlap with “Premiere Pro… Livestream studio workflows” in Technical + IT; keep this section capability-focused.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level and relevance, e.g.: **Drupal (enterprise, migration and microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put the strongest/recent platform first and make Drupal clearly dominant, since it underpins the most recent and highest-impact work.
- Standardize naming for professionalism: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of just Power Pages.
- If space allows elsewhere, add light qualifiers rather than more tools: **Drupal 10, enterprise publishing, modular content architecture**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one list or differentiating this one with proficiency/context.
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight versus the enterprise/public-sector positioning unless it supports a specific project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant stack for your recent web modernization work, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and modernity, while aligning with the more senior, systems-focused positioning elsewhere in the CV.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a concise capability line: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery; technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use versioning; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- Group tools by function rather than listing flatly; this improves scanability and signals practical application.
- If accurate, add one specificity cue tied to recent work, e.g. “serverless scripting,” “deployment automation,” or “tagging implementation” to show applied use, not just familiarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; consider keeping detail here and shortening the topline version.
- “API integrations” and “workflow automation” are already implied elsewhere, so avoid repeating both in multiple sections verbatim.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from app list to capability-led grouping: **Workflow automation & work management:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp
- Move collaboration tools out of this item if possible: **Slack, Teams** fit better under a separate “Collaboration” label or can be removed
- If space allows, add light context to show level: **Built and managed workflow systems in Airtable; automated cross-team processes with Power Automate and Zapier**
- Consider ordering by relevance/strength, with Airtable and automation tools first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap as project-management tools; listing all four may feel padded unless each was used meaningfully

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength from recent roles: enterprise email operations and member communications. It should signal scale or use case, not just list tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise newsletter operations • Member communications workflows**
- If accurate, add light context in parentheses: **Higher Logic (member association email)** • **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration)**  
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was minimal/older exposure, move it down or remove it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated “email/newsletters reaching tens of thousands” in Work Experience, so avoid adding outcome claims here unless tied to platform-specific capability.
- “Engagement” is broad; don’t imply CRM/marketing automation depth beyond what your experience bullets support.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content execution, and any concrete scale/results.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten scope and reduce generic phrasing: replace “strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia” with specific contributions such as publishing operations, content production, or channel coordination.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: size of website refresh, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience growth, email/social engagement, or team size.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting publishing operations across web, email, social and video. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while informally supervising a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this entry more execution-focused.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, clearer scope, and a sharper emphasis on outcomes or organizational value.

Suggested edit
- Recast to foreground the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Tighten the first sentence to specify function and audience: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy programs and member-facing organizational priorities.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer ownership: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, stakeholders supported, programs served, or audience/reach.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “multimedia production” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and innovation/research support.
- Since later roles cover digital operations in depth, don’t overstate this item as a full digital leadership role.
